expected_level_description: You can: - define the integration build - co-ordinate build activities across systems - understand how to undertake and support integration testing activities

You can: - collaborate with others when necessary to review specifications - use the agreed specifications to design, code, test and document programs or scripts of medium-to-high complexity, using the right standards and tools

You can: - translate logical designs into physical designs - produce detailed designs - effectively document all work using required standards, methods and tools, including prototyping tools where appropriate - design systems characterised by managed levels of risk, manageable business and technical complexity, and meaningful impact - work with well understood technology and identify appropriate patterns
You can: - identify, locate and fix service faults
You can: - use information security practices and available security controls to contribute to protecting solutions and services

You can: - design and build integrations using FHIR, HL7 version 2, and messaging patterns - write and profile FHIR resources and implementation guides - resolve complex mapping and data quality issues between systems
You can: - find and use the right codes for a data item or form - use terminology browsers and reference sets
You can: - apply data protection principles to your work - contribute to data protection impact assessments - handle information requests and records correctly
You can: - take part in hazard workshops and contribute to a hazard log - follow the clinical risk management process for your work - provide evidence for a clinical safety case, such as test results

You can: - explain the clinical and care workflows your work supports - use common health care terms correctly with clinical and care colleagues - recognise when a change could affect patient care and raise it
